summary: Kept the valley of ashes, Eckleburg, Wilson garage, Myrtle's transformation, the 'You can't live forever' and 'Daisy!' passages, the broken nose, and the Beauty-and-the-Beast coda largely verbatim; compressed the dog sale, apartment furnishings, McKee chatter and Catherine's talk into condensed or summarized passages.
acceptable_changes: Catherine's Monte Carlo tangent and most of the McKees' dialogue (Mrs. McKee's gossip, Mr. McKee's Montauk studies) were cut or reduced, per the cuttable inventory.
Catherine's Catholic lie was kept only in minimal form because Nick's 'Daisy was not a Catholic' reaction depends on it.
The McKees and Catherine are glossed locally on first appearance, and the elevator exchange is kept so the closing Beauty-and-the-Beast fragment still lands.
risks: The dog-purchase dialogue is partly paraphrased, which loses some of the old man's comic patter.
Myrtle's 'borrowed suit' anecdote and her 'crazy about him' exchange are shortened, which may thin the marriage-disappointment material.
'Mr. McKee' is used without his first name, and the abridgment never says he is a photographer from the flat below until introduced; check the gloss reads clearly.
Dialogue in the McKee photographing exchange was condensed with attribution kept; check speaker clarity.
review_focus: Confirm the compressed Catherine/Catholic passage still sets up Nick's reaction to the lie about Daisy.
Check that the Eckleburg and valley-of-ashes paragraphs and the 'within and without' sentence are verbatim.
Verify the transition at Tom's 'George B. Wilson at the Gasoline Pump' joke reads smoothly after the cut.
